summary: Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna (1965–1972). He served as a university lecturer at the University of Vienna starting in 1969 and held a research stay at the University of Madras (1972–1974).

V. Kameswari is an Indologist associated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where she served as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as a supervisor and guide (attested 2026).

Vinayaka P. Bhatta is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He has held positions at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as head of the Sanskrit Dictionary Project (attested 2011) and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).

V. R. Srinivasan is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who was attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

V. Raghavan was an Indologist who studied at Presidency College, Chennai, and the University of Madras (Ph.D. 1934) under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He worked at the University of Madras (1934–1968) and served as secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (~1944–1979).

V. W. Paranjpe was an Indologist and linguist who served as Superintendent of the Publication Department at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1927) and later as Professor Emeritus at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1984, 2007).
Vaibhav Singh is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Reading in 2017 and held a post there (attested 2018).

Valaiyattur Venkayya was an epigraphist and scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology educated at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He served as acting Government Epigraphist of Madras (~1903–1908) and Acting Government Epigraphist for the Archaeological Survey of India (1905).

Valdo H. Viglielmo was a Japanologist and philosopher who earned degrees at Harvard (A.B. 1946, M.A. 1956) and studied in Tokyo. He taught at Harvard, Meiji Gakuin, and Princeton, before serving as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1965–2002).

Valeria Gazizova is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Oslo, completing a master's thesis under the supervision of Per Kværne, and also studied under Hanna Havnevik.

Valerie Hansen is a historian and sinologist who studied at Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair. She has served at Yale University as an associate professor (~1993–1998) and as a Professor of History (~1998–present).

Valerie Stoker is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who holds a post at Wright State University. She studied under traditional teachers D. Prahladachar and Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi.
Vamana was a scholar in the field of Indology who studied under traditional teachers Keshava, Dattatreya Sastri Nigudkar, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.
Vamanshastri Kinjawadekar was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under traditional teachers Dattatreya, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.

Van Austin Harvey was a philosopher of religion who earned his B.D. and Ph.D. at Yale. He served as department chair at Southern Methodist University (1958–1968) and the University of Pennsylvania (1968–1978), and was a professor at Stanford University (~1978–1996).
Vans Kennedy was an Indologist and linguist who served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army (1817–1835) and later as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1846).

Vasant Shinde is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He has served as Professor and Professor of South Asian Archaeology at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2006, 2026).

Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev was a sinologist who studied at St. Petersburg University and under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1910–1951) and the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1918–1951).

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied under Józef Kowalewski at Kazan State University (~1833–1837). He served as professor at Kazan (1851) and Saint Petersburg State University (1855–1893).

Vasily Radlov was a linguist, historian, and Central Asian specialist who earned his doctorate at Jena (1858). He served as director of the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and director of the Kunstkamera (1894–1918).
